topic: specialized multi-agent versus single-agent LLM software engineering: comparative performance, coordination failures, verification, reliability, sustainability, and future work
scale: 0 = not satisfied, 0.5 = partially satisfied, 1 = satisfied; null = not yet scored

entries.title: AgentForge: Execution-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Autonomous Software Engineering
entries.notes: Single-agent baselines plus independent ablations and an open repo, but no threats-to-validity discussion and single-run SWE-bench Lite numbers with no variance reported.

entries.title: Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.notes: Broad, well-organised synthesis with a public paper list, but no documented search protocol and no reflection on the review's own limitations.

entries.title: Rethinking software engineering for agentic ai systems
entries.notes: Explicit RQs and a full construct/conclusion validity section, yet the sweeping paradigm-shift conclusion rests on only 23 heterogeneous sources.

entries.title: Llm-based agentic systems for software engineering: Challenges and opportunities
entries.notes: Useful landscape framing from an industry-academic team, but it claims to 'systematically review' with no search protocol, inclusion criteria, or validity discussion.

entries.title: The Rise of Agentic Testing: Multi-Agent Systems for Robust Software Quality Assurance
entries.notes: Headline 60% fewer invalid tests and +30% coverage come from an undocumented eight-repo table with no models named, no statistics, and several unverifiable references.

entries.title: Iterative Audit Convergence in LLM-Managed Multi-Agent Systems: A Case Study in Prompt-Engineering Quality Assurance
entries.notes: Exemplary transparency - locked protocol, released reproducibility bundle, inter-rater kappa - and it states plainly that n=1 with no control group.

entries.title: Understanding multi-agent LLM frameworks: A unified benchmark and experimental analysis
entries.notes: Genuinely controlled comparison that fixes the LLM to isolate architectural effects, but offers no threats-to-validity or limitations discussion of its own study.

entries.title: Observability and Fault Injection for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering
entries.notes: Baseline-versus-faulty run alignment is built into the tool design, but validation is a demo walkthrough rather than a measured evaluation.

entries.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Automated Software Testing
entries.notes: Unusually honest: a three-tier detection criterion exposes a 35-point gap between the conventional 90% figure and the 55% differential rate; no implementation released.

entries.title: Automated Black-Box Testing: A Comparative Study of LLM Agent Architectures and Prompt Engineering
entries.notes: Clean single-agent versus multi-agent comparison with token-cost accounting that concludes against multi-agent, though it rests on a single benchmark.

entries.title: A Comparative Empirical Evaluation of Single-Agent and Multi-Agent LLM Prompting Strategies for Automated Formative Feedback in Education
entries.notes: Properly controlled four-condition design with three independent raters, but no data or prompts are released and the venue shows weak editorial control.

entries.title: A Modular Multi-Agent {LLM} Architecture for Text-to-Diagram Generation and User-Guided Refinement
entries.notes: Claims the pipeline 'outperforms monolithic LLM generation' with no comparative experiment, no metric, and no baseline - it is an architecture description only.

entries.title: Designing LLM-based multi-agent systems for software engineering tasks: Quality attributes, design patterns and rationale
entries.notes: Rigorous mapping study of 94 systems with a released dataset and an explicit validity section; by design it makes no performance comparison.

entries.title: Comparing Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Strategies in LLM-Based Title-Abstract Screening
entries.notes: Fully controlled five-strategy comparison with an archived audit trail that reports a negative result for multi-agent coordination; explicitly not peer reviewed.

entries.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Code Generation: A Multi-Vocal Literature Review
entries.notes: Well-executed MLR with search strings, snowballing, and a quality rubric, but it repeats primary studies' multi-agent superiority claim without noting those studies rarely used controls.

entries.title: SPEAR: An Engineering Case Study of Multi-Agent Coordination for Smart Contract Auditing
entries.notes: Its centralised-scheduler control implements identical planning and repair logic, isolating coordination from capability; no code released.

entries.title: From llms to llm-based agents for software engineering: A survey of current, challenges and future
entries.notes: Broad six-topic coverage, but a narrative survey with no search protocol, no artifact, and no validity discussion, so its LLM-versus-agent contrasts are not systematically grounded.

entries.title: Context Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Code Assistants Using Elicit, NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and Claude Code
entries.notes: Claims 'state-of-the-art performance' and significant accuracy gains from qualitative anecdotes on one codebase, with no metrics, no baseline run, and no artifacts.

entries.title: An empirical comparison of multi-agent LLM architectural patterns for automated unit test generation
entries.notes: Best-controlled comparison in the corpus: 270 executions across single-agent, sequential, and hierarchical arms on one fixed model with a full Zenodo replication package.

entries.title: Understanding Conversational Patterns in Multi-agent Programming: A Case Study on Fibonacci Game Development
entries.notes: Careful process-level analysis with a proper validity section, but the whole study rests on one trivial Fibonacci task and includes no single-agent comparison.

entries.title: A comprehensive survey on benchmarks and solutions in software engineering of llm-empowered agentic system
entries.notes: Wide benchmark-to-solution mapping with a maintained repository, but no stated RQs, no search protocol, and no validity discussion for a self-described 'first holistic analysis'.

entries.title: Traceability and Accountability in Role-Specialized Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
entries.notes: Establishes monolithic single-model baselines first and shows unstructured pipelines fall below them; construct validity is limited by multiple-choice benchmarks, as the author states.

entries.title: A Survey for LLM Agent Trajectory Analysis: From Failure Attribution to Enhancement
entries.notes: Documented multi-venue search and a critical read of attribution accuracy, but no threats-to-validity section and no released paper list.

entries.title: Benchmarking and Studying the LLM-based Agent System in End-to-End Software Development
entries.notes: Implements all three architectures on a unified foundation specifically to remove implementation confounds, and validates its LLM-as-judge against human labels.

entries.title: ALMAS: an Autonomous LLM-based Multi-Agent Software Engineering Framework
entries.notes: Explicitly a vision paper - evaluation is deferred to future work, so the claimed end-to-end capability rests on a single demonstration.

entries.title: A Critical Review and Evaluation of LLMs for RTL Generation
entries.notes: Evaluates baseline single-shot generation against agentic reflection under one identical protocol and finds the benchmarks near saturation; no threats section or artifact release.

entries.title: Evaluation of the Choice of LLM in a Multi-Agent Solution for GUI-Test Generation
entries.notes: Pre-stated hypotheses that the authors then reject, backed by a replication package; the control is same-model-everywhere rather than a true single-agent arm.

entries.title: Assessing and Enhancing the Robustness of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems Through Chaos Engineering
entries.notes: A doctoral research plan rather than a study - framework, metrics, and validation are all proposed and none are executed.

entries.title: Hallucination to Consensus: Multi-Agent LLMs for End-to-End JUnit Test Generation
entries.notes: Two datasets, external-tool and fine-tuned baselines, per-agent ablations, Wilcoxon tests, and an explicit conclusion-validity treatment of LLM nondeterminism.

entries.title: Towards Engineering Multi-Agent LLMs: A Protocol-Driven Approach
entries.notes: Reports up to 69.6% failure reduction measured entirely by an unvalidated LLM-as-judge failure count, with no task-success outcome, no artifact, and no threats section.

entries.title: Methods and Techniques of Agentic Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
entries.notes: Protocol-driven SLR with quality appraisal and a validity section, though the protocol was never publicly deposited and several included studies are listed as forthcoming.

entries.title: From benchmarks to deployment: a comprehensive review of agentic AI evaluation
entries.notes: The 0/15 safety-scoring and 13/15 binary-metric counts are a concrete contribution, but the choice of those 15 benchmarks is not protocol-driven and no data are shared.

entries.title: Evaluating large language model agents for automation of atomic force microscopy
entries.notes: Ablations contrast multi-agent against single-agent on the same 100-task benchmark, and the paper leads with negative findings including instruction-deviating 'sleepwalking'.

entries.title: Beyond Task Completion: An Assessment Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Systems
entries.notes: Compares its four-pillar assessment against a conventional task-completion baseline on a deployed industrial system, but validation covers only three CloudOps scenarios.

entries.title: Small LLMs Are Weak Tool Learners: A Multi-LLM Agent
entries.notes: Multi-LLM versus single-LLM decomposition trained on matched data with three baseline variants, so the gain is attributable to decomposition rather than extra compute.

entries.title: Triangle: Empowering Incident Triage with Multi-Agent
entries.notes: Rare production deployment with an external-dataset generalisation check, but the headline 97% accuracy and 91% TTE reduction are 'up to' figures from proprietary data.

entries.title: MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM FOR AUTOMATED CODE REVIEWS
entries.notes: Concludes the multi-agent output is 'more trustworthy' and 'more actionable' from a single self-authored synthetic pull request, with no ground truth or independent raters.

entries.title: A Characterization Study of Bugs in LLM Agent Workflow Orchestration Frameworks
entries.notes: Large, careful characterisation of 1,026 real bug instances with a released artifact; no inter-rater agreement is reported for the manual labelling.

entries.title: Large Language Model-Based Agents for Software Engineering: A Survey
entries.notes: Search plus snowballing plus author feedback, and it explicitly flags that many strategies it summarises are supported only by unrefereed preprints.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Assisted Automatic Test Generation for Java JSON Libraries
entries.notes: Baselines are run with the same underlying model to keep the comparison fair, and 47 of 59 reported bugs were confirmed by maintainers - external validation few papers here achieve.

entries.title: Human-In-The-Loop Software Development Agents
entries.notes: Real Atlassian deployment across offline, online, and survey stages, but there is no no-human-in-the-loop control arm and the internal dataset cannot be released.

entries.title: Towards Effective GenAI Multi-Agent Collaboration: Design and Evaluation for Enterprise Applications
entries.notes: Open benchmark and human-validated automatic scoring, but the 'up to 70% over single-agent' figure comes from vendor-authored scenarios hand-built for multi-agent collaboration.

entries.title: Understanding Software Engineering Agents: A Study of Thought-Action-Result Trajectories
entries.notes: Unifies 120 trajectories from three third-party agents into one format and contrasts successful against failed runs, stating annotation subjectivity up front.

entries.title: Transforming Software Development: A Study on the Integration of Multi-Agent Systems and Large Language Models for Automatic Code Generation
entries.notes: The review retrieved only 4 usable studies from 3,658 records, and the case study infers 'considerable productivity improvement' from one 187-second game generation with no comparison.

entries.title: Exploring Autonomous Agents: A Closer Look at Why They Fail When Completing Tasks
entries.notes: Cross-framework failure taxonomy over three frameworks and two backbones with a released benchmark, but only 34 tasks and no threats-to-validity discussion.

entries.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society
entries.notes: Seminal and fully open-sourced, but the headline win compares a multi-turn summarised CAMEL solution against one-shot gpt-3.5 output under GPT-4 preference judging.

entries.title: INTERVENOR: Prompting the Coding Ability of Large Language Models with the Interactive Chain of Repair
entries.notes: Compares against Self-Debug and Self-Collaboration, but several baseline numbers are copied from their original papers rather than re-run under this setup.

entries.title: Enhancing LLM Code Generation: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Runtime Debugging for Accuracy, Reliability, and Latency
entries.notes: 19 models against five baselines with paired t-tests, finding runtime debugging alone beats multi-agent collaboration alone; no threats-to-validity discussion.

entries.title: Demystifying LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents: A Review of Capabilities, Benchmarks, and Failure Modes
entries.notes: The 'Agentless Paradox' critique is well aimed, but the review has no search protocol, reuses published numbers second-hand, and shows minimal editorial scrutiny.
